messages:
nina: Quick design check: onboarding users are confused by the rules editor preview. They expect to see a before/after diff when reordering but only get a static list. Also 'Invalid order' toast keeps popping during tests. Screenshot + user quote attached.

omar: onboarding tooltip idea: add a small inline "How reordering works" helper with a 3-frame micro-animation showing drag -> placeholder -> dropped. Keep it optional (dismissible).

felix: For the validation toast, prefer clearer phrasing: "Ordering blocked — unresolved dependencies" or "Action blocked — view dependency list". Include a secondary action "Show affected rules" that opens the dependency popover.

maria: Design nit: priority number should live in a narrow left rail so it never shifts during drag. When a rule is disabled, switch to a left-aligned pill with icon rather than strike-through only. This helps eyeballing long stacks.

sam: Accessibility + behaviour: aria-live (polite) should announce keyboard moves like: "Moved ‘Throttle external calls’ to position 3 of 12". Also include an undo snackbar after programmatic auto-resolve of conflicts.

a11y-bot: reminder: disabled state cannot rely on color alone. Contrast ratios for disabled small text must be >= 4.5:1 unless accompanied by another indicator (icon, pill, pattern). Test with screen reader flows for reorder.

omar: animation: subtle slide + highlight destination for 180ms. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by falling back to instant placement. CSS prototype: ```css .rule { transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.3,1); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .rule { transition: none; } } ```

felix: UX for auto-inserted fallback rules: show a non-modal inline banner in the preview with "Why this rule was added" link. Clicking shows a diff and an "Accept suggestion" CTA. If user accepts, push change to top-of-stack? maybe better to show suggested position and require confirm.

maria: Mobile gesture note: long-press drag conflicts with swipe-to-delete on small screens. For mobile, expose an explicit grab handle and offer a compact reorder modal listing rules with drag handles.

sam: Performance: virtualize long lists but keep the visible index numbers stable. On drag, render a sticky clone of the dragged item to avoid reflows.

a11y-bot: also ensure focus returns to moved item and that aria-owns is updated for the list ordering.

deploy-bot: tiny UX canary deployed: https://staging.redwood.com/routing/editor/friendly-onboarding

nina: Thanks. Let's do a short 10min usability test on Friday to validate: onboarding micro-anim, new validation copy, and mobile reorder modal. Bring recordings and contrast checks.
